newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Teva says its Copaxone drug doing well in U.S..
newsitem.headline: Teva says its Copaxone drug doing well in U.S..

text.p: Israel's Teva Pharmaceutical Industries Ltd said on Monday its treatment for multiple sclerosis (MS) is capturing the majority of new prescriptions in the United States.

"We feel that we have the majority of new prescriptions. More new patients are selecting Copaxone over the competition," chief financial officer Dan Suesskind told Reuters after the company announced sharply higher second-quarter earnings.
"It is more than a feeling," he said. "It is an extrapolation we feel is right."

Teva began marketing Copaxone in the United States in the second quarter. The company estimates over 4,000 MS patients in the United States are being treated with its drug and that this number is growing by more than 1,000 new patients a month.

Teva officials said they could not disclose more precise information at this time. In a July report, Lehman Brothers estimated Copaxone has captured 23 percent of new prescriptions, including home health care distribution.

Teva's earnings in the second quarter jumped to $0.55 a share, in line with analysts' expectations, against $0.01 a share a year earlier. The 1996 quarter included a one-time expense of $0.24 a share for the acquisition of Biocraft Laboratories in May of last year.
The second quarter of 1996 did not include sales of APS/Berk, a British company Teva acquired in July 1996. Teva said this company has not yet contributed to profits.
Suesskind said that without the introduction of Copaxone second-quarter earnings would have been higher.

"We knew from the beginning the impact (of Copaxone) this year would not be great," president and chief executive Eli Hurvitz told a news conference. "Next year we will see a significant contribution from Copaxone."
Teva also declared a dividend for the quarter of 0.30 shekels a share to be paid on September 11.

The rise in net profit outpaced sales growth, reflecting an erosion in prices on the one hand and the penetration of new products and a rise in market share for existing products on the other hand, the company said. Profitability also rose due to synergies realised from the acquisition of Biocraft.
Exports rose 28.4 percent in the quarter to $198.31 million, against an 11.4 percent increase in domestic sales to $72.36 million.
North America continued to account for half of Teva's sales while sales in Europe jumped 42.4 percent to $47.39 million.

Net research and development expenses rose 23 percent in the quarter to $15 million. The company is developing a number of products relating to the central nervous and immunity systems. Teva is engaged in Phase III trials in the United States for a treatment for Parkinson's disease called Rasagiline.
